Variant Picker shows a product’s options the way shoppers expect: colors as swatches, sizes as buttons, never a dropdown that hides what’s in stock. It works out every option from the variants you pass, so each value knows whether it’s available, sold out or not made in the current combination.

VariantAvailability reads the chosen variant as In stock, Only 3 left, Pre-order with the ship date, or Backordered. NotifyMe collects an email for a sold-out variant. The helpers, findVariant, getOptionStates, getInitialSelection, getPriceRange and the search param pair, work on their own, on the server too.

fromShopify maps a Storefront API product to Product: swatch colors and images, prices and stock come across as they are, and availableForSale, currentlyNotInStock and quantityAvailable become the availability state.
selectionFromSearchParams and selectionToSearchParams read and write ?color=Oat&size=King, so a shared link opens the same variant and Back restores it. Values that aren’t in the product are dropped.
validate() flags and focuses the first missing option and returns whether every option is chosen.
validate() sets aria-invalid and links the error text to the group, then moves focus into it. Status is never shown by color alone: sold out has a line and words, and stock has words next to its dot.
